discovery: Neutron-star mergers as sites of r-process nucleosynthesis and the theory of r-process-powered kilonovae

nominees.name: Brian D. Metzger
nominees.affiliation: Columbia University and Flatiron Institute, USA

nominees.name: Daniel Kasen
nominees.affiliation: University of California, Berkeley and Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, USA

motivation: Where the elements heavier than iron were made was a long-standing open question. Lattimer first proposed, with the late D. N. Schramm, that neutron-rich matter ejected when a neutron star is tidally disrupted by a compact companion undergoes rapid neutron capture. Metzger showed that the radioactive decay of freshly synthesized r-process nuclei powers a distinctive transient, the kilonova, and predicted its luminosity and timescale. Kasen showed that the very high opacity of lanthanides makes kilonovae red and long-lived, which made the prediction quantitative and testable. Their framework was confirmed spectacularly by the optical and infrared counterpart of GW170817. Today it links nuclear masses, half-lives and fission properties of exotic nuclei measured at radioactive-beam facilities directly to observed light curves and to cosmic heavy-element abundances. It turned the origin of gold and uranium into a quantitative science.
